name: Euronet Worldwide

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Moves money and cash three ways: ATMs and card processing, prepaid mobile/digital content distribution, and cross-border transfers (Ria, Xe, Dandelion). Two plain sentences; model is clear.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: 9M 2026 revenue $3,281M: Cross-Border $1,296M (39%), Payments Infrastructure (ATMs, Ren, merchant acquiring, CoreCard) $1,110M (34%), epay $882M (27%). 9M op income: PI $238M, epay $97M, Cross-Border $123M (-28%).

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: No customer above 10% of revenue in any segment; buyers are consumers, banks, retailers, mobile operators. Walmart is a named Ria sending agent.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: ATMs in 70 countries, largely Europe, Asia and Middle East; Ria strongest in US-outbound corridors. Translation risk: 2025 op income was 4.1% higher from FX, so a strong dollar now reverses that (euro avg +4% y/y in 9M, but euro -2% q/q).

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Per-transaction fees plus FX margin; ATM fees and DCC (currency conversion) at the cash machine; prepaid commissions. Mostly paid per use, not subscription; digital accelerators are 26% of YTD revenue and +33%.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Q3 revenue +1% but op income -12%: costs are sticky (salaries and SG&A up). Capex $125.5M in 2025 (3% of revenue). Q3 guidance miss and outlook cut in October; investor-day targets from May revised after five months.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical inputs: bank/network sponsors and Visa/Mastercard rules for ATM interchange, agent networks (about 654,000 Ria locations), local payout partners, cash for ATMs ($913M ATM cash funded by debt), mobile operators and content brands for epay. No single supplier named as critical; chokepoints are card-network rules and payout partners. Cost pass-through: weak in remittance (Western Union has twice the revenue and price pressure), moderate in epay, limited in ATMs (cost inflation hit PI margin). Signal tags: dollar (translation), travel_airlines (tourist ATM volume), rates (ATM cash funding), regulation (remittance tax, DCC rules).

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Owned global payout network, Ren software, 'Dandelion' real-time payments rail, scale in ATMs. Doing differently: digital transactions in Cross-Border +34% to 8.1M in Q3; letter of intent with Diebold Nixdorf. Retail cash remittance edge is not strong against Western Union.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Ria and Euronet ATMs are visible to immigrant communities and tourists but are not a household name; people would switch ATM or sender with little notice.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Cross-Border transactions -2% to 45.3M while digital +34%; Western Union has about 2x Ria's revenue. ATMs +4% (59,688 installed), epay transactions +4%. Share in US retail remittance is under pressure from policy, not clearly from rivals.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Digital accelerators +33% YTD (Ria digital, merchant acquiring, Ren); CoreCard (acquired Q4 2025) lifts PI. Runway real but small against the retail remittance decline; 9M group revenue only +4.6%.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: FCF (operating cash flow less capex) 2021-25: $314M, $644M, $549M, $616M, $434M; 9M 2026 about $161M vs $288M a year earlier. Bought back $200M in 9M 2026 (more than 9M FCF). Debt $2,177M, unrestricted cash $955M, investment-grade stated aim. Insiders hold 12.2% (CEO 6.8%). Pay: 40% cumulative adjusted op income, 24% adjusted EPS growth, 36% stock price. Rough ROIC about 11% vs 10% hurdle.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Retail cash remittance is a shrinking pool under US immigration and tax policy; ATM travel volume depends on tourists. Digital shift is under way, so not a Zoom case, but the cash-based core is losing relevance while the digital core is not yet big enough.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 4.01 or 4.02 items, no NT filing, no material weakness (controls effective at 12/31/2025), one critical audit matter on revenue evidence (routine). Sept 2025 CORRESP was an S-4 acceleration request, not a comment letter. Adjusted measures exclude a small non-cash accrual only.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: mixed (inflation helps nominal fees; strong dollar and tighter rates hurt translation and ATM cash cost). Slowdown: tourism and remittance volumes soften, but epay is steadier. Dollar +4.8% in 3 months is a headwind; outlook excludes further FX moves.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Cross-Border explicitly cites US immigration policy and the US remittance tax as the cause of the decline; Q3 not fully recovered ('market remains fragile'). DCC rules in the EU are a second exposure. No pending merger docket found.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $69.07 (market cap $2.54B, 36.7M shares). Reverse DCF at 10% discount, 3% terminal: on 2025 FCF of $434M the price implies FCF shrinking about 10% a year for 10 years; on $300M it implies -5%; flat FCF is justified only if FCF is about $215M. Own FCF growth 2021-25 was +8%/yr (but 2022-25 fell). Multiples: GAAP P/E 11.4 trailing; EV/adjusted EBITDA about 5.2x on $725M guide (EV about $3.76B before netting ATM cash). Peers: WU trailing P/E 6.0, RM 6.6. Own 5-year multiple range not computed; the stock is 53% below its 5-year high ($146).

status_reason: Price leaves a large cushion, but quality is C and earnings are still falling (Q3 op income -12%, outlook cut) until US remittance volumes turn.
the_mistake: The market prices Euronet as one shrinking cash-remittance and tourist-ATM business; ATMs (+4%), epay (+3% revenue) and digital transfers (+34%) are growing and the stock implies cash flow falling about 10% a year. The risk is that the remittance drop is policy-driven and may last.
what_makes_market_notice: Stabilising US remittance volumes (Q3 sequential decline already narrowed from -5% to -4%); Q4 2026 results (expected February 2027, date not confirmed); digital accelerators passing 30% of revenue.

feedback.fact: Management says US immigration-related pressure on remittances 'persisted longer than we anticipated', and the revised outlook cites FX conversion rate changes; ATM volumes face 'economic pressures on discretionary travel spend'. Supports Overheat-with-turn-risk: real consumer pressure and strong dollar are showing up in cross-border flows.
